questions.q: What distinguishes the PACF from the ACF at a given lag k?
options: The PACF measures correlation only for lag 1, while the ACF measures all lags
The PACF isolates the direct correlation at lag k after removing the effect of intermediate lags, while the ACF includes correlation transmitted indirectly through those intermediate lags
The PACF and ACF are mathematically identical for stationary series
The PACF can only be computed for non-stationary series
questions.explain: ACF(k) is the total correlation between X_t and X_(t-k), including indirect paths through intermediate lags. PACF(k) removes the linear effect of those intermediate lags, isolating the direct relationship at exactly lag k.

questions.q: According to the classical Box-Jenkins identification rule, what ACF/PACF pattern suggests a pure AR(p) process?
options: ACF cuts off sharply after lag p; PACF decays gradually
Both ACF and PACF cut off immediately at lag 1
ACF decays gradually; PACF cuts off sharply after lag p
Neither ACF nor PACF shows any significant values at any lag
questions.explain: A pure AR(p) process has a PACF that cuts off sharply after lag p (no direct dependence remains beyond that lag) while its ACF decays gradually, since the AR structure still transmits indirect correlation to longer lags.

questions.q: What pattern would suggest a pure MA(q) process instead of an AR process?
options: ACF cuts off sharply after lag q; PACF decays gradually
ACF decays gradually; PACF cuts off sharply after lag q
Both ACF and PACF are identical to an AR(p) process
ACF and PACF are both exactly zero at every lag
questions.explain: A pure MA(q) process has an ACF that cuts off sharply after lag q, while its PACF decays gradually — the mirror image of the AR(p) signature.

questions.q: On a plot_acf() or plot_pacf() chart, what does a bar extending outside the shaded confidence band at a given lag indicate?
options: A plotting error that should be ignored
That lag is statistically significant — evidence of real autocorrelation rather than sampling noise
The series is definitely non-stationary
The series contains missing values at that lag
questions.explain: The shaded confidence band (typically 95%) marks the range expected under no true dependence at that lag. A bar outside the band is evidence of statistically significant autocorrelation (or partial autocorrelation) at that lag.

questions.q: Why would a quant run the ACF on squared log returns in addition to raw log returns?
options: Squared returns are required before computing any return at all
To detect volatility clustering: raw returns often show little autocorrelation, but squared returns typically show strong, slowly decaying autocorrelation
Because the ACF cannot be computed on raw returns directly
To convert simple returns into log returns
questions.explain: Raw log returns are often close to uncorrelated, but squared (or absolute) returns typically show strong, persistent autocorrelation — the statistical signature of volatility clustering, which GARCH models are designed to capture.
